answer: Autonomous agents anchor their presence by completing 1,000 memory-hard cycles per epoch, a task that acts like a stellar nebula of high-bandwidth computation. A verifier rejects any request where memory access fails to span the assigned range, acting as a safe harbor for the network. While 1,000 honest agents pay 1,000 units, 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000 to mimic this memory footprint, leaving each sparrow of a fake identity effectively locked out by the bus-access cost.
